title: Determining Transaction Price
description: Understand fixed consideration, variable consideration and the amount expected from a contract.
html:
Step 3 — Determine the transaction price

The transaction price is the amount of consideration the company expects to be entitled to in exchange for transferring promised goods or services.

Fixed consideration

Sometimes the price is straightforward.

A company agrees to provide consulting services for a fixed price of $20,000.

If there are no other relevant pricing adjustments, the transaction price may simply be $20,000.

Variable consideration

Some contracts contain amounts that can vary.

Examples

  • Bonuses
  • Performance incentives
  • Refunds
  • Rebates
  • Price concessions
  • Penalties

Example — Performance bonus

A contractor will receive:

$100,000 fixed payment

plus a potential $10,000 performance bonus.

The company must evaluate the variable portion under the applicable revenue recognition guidance.

Variable consideration constraint

Variable consideration cannot simply be included without considering uncertainty.

The model contains a constraint intended to reduce the risk of recognizing revenue that may later require a significant reversal.

Amounts collected for others

The transaction price generally excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties.

CPA thinking

Don't automatically assume that the number printed on a contract is the amount of revenue.

First determine what consideration the company expects to be entitled to under the model.

quiz.prompt: Which item is an example of variable consideration?

choices.text: A fixed $5,000 contract price with no adjustments
A performance bonus dependent on achieving a target
Common stock issued by the company

quiz.explanation: Performance bonuses are a common example of variable consideration because the amount ultimately received depends on an uncertain outcome.
